title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task, the Brain Invaders video game, at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2013. It was designed to compare a P300-based BCI with and without adaptive calibration using Riemannian geometry. Each participant completed eight sessions, each with adaptive and non-adaptive runs. This version is a BIDS-formatted derivative produced with MOABB.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 16 wet Ag/AgCl electrodes (g.tec g.USBamp, g.GAMMAcap) with a left earlobe reference and OpenViBE software. Each session had two runs, Non-Adaptive and Adaptive, in randomised order. Each run had a Training (calibration) phase and an Online phase. The Training phase had 80 Target and 400 non-Target flashes. The interface presented 36 symbols in 12 groups, and subjects were blind to the mode of operation. Stimulus tags were sent to the amplifier via USB.
